questions.feedbackIfWrong: When events are mutually exclusive, P(A or B) = P(A) + P(B).
questions.prompt: Which formula gives the probability of A or B when A and B are mutually exclusive?

questions.feedbackIfWrong: Events that cannot occur together are mutually exclusive.
questions.prompt: Two events that cannot occur at the same time are called ___ exclusive.
If P(A) = 0.3, P(B) = 0.4, and A and B are mutually exclusive, find P(A or B). (Give decimal.)
Which pair of events is mutually exclusive?
options: Rolling a 3 and rolling a 4 on one die
Selecting a heart and selecting a king from a deck
Being a male and being a nursing major
Having brown eyes and having black hair
questions.feedbackIfWrong: Rolling a 3 and rolling a 4 on the same roll are mutually exclusive.
Subtract P(A and B) to avoid double-counting the overlap.
questions.prompt: The Addition Rule for events that are not mutually exclusive is P(A or B) = P(A) + P(B) - ___.
Why do we subtract P(A and B) in the general Addition Rule? (Answer: to avoid ___)
questions.feedbackIfWrong: We subtract P(A and B) to avoid double-counting.

questions.prompt: P(puncture) = 0.05, P(smashed corner) = 0.08, P(both) = 0.004. Find P(puncture or smashed corner).
The complement of 'A or B' is 'not A and ___ B'.
questions.feedbackIfWrong: The complement is 'not A and not B'.

questions.prompt: If P(A or B) = 0.35, what is P(neither A nor B)? (Give decimal.)

The notation $ n! $ is read as 'n ___'.
Compute $ 5! \div 3! $.

options: Arranging the letters of a word
Choosing a committee from a group

questions.prompt: Which of the following situations involves a combination?
How many ways can you choose 2 students from a group of 10?
For a combination, order ___ not matter.
questions.feedbackIfWrong: Order does not matter in a combination.
